looped2sH264.reading: W3: WebKitGTK plays the first loop iteration (~1s), restarts at 0, then stalls forever (paused=false, readyState 4, no error). totalVideoFrames 60 = exactly one 2s x 30fps iteration decoded. Chromium loops fine.

noLoop6sH264.reading: Non-looped playback is realtime on BOTH engines. WebKit drops 0/179 frames even at loadavg 22; Chromium drops 62/180 under the same load. The stall is loop-specific, not a decode failure.

webglShaderValidated.reading: Same shader, same output pixels on both engines (center pixel 20 vs 22 light, 239 vs 233 heavy). Chromium median 0ms at BOTH sizes is NOT real speed: 92M sin/cos pairs cannot execute in <0.5ms on CPU, so ANGLE/Vulkan defers the work past gl.finish() (multi-process GPU path) and this method cannot measure Chromium WebGL cost. WebKit scales linearly with work (91ms at 6.9M pairs, 1394ms at 92M pairs) = synchronous software rasterization, ~70M trig pairs/s. Do NOT quote Chromium 0ms as a speed number.
